root_cause.text: The SEV ioctl handler `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2()` in `drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c` copied `data.len` bytes from the kernel `id_blob` to userspace even when the PSP/firmware command had failed, allowing firmware-updated length values to exceed the allocated buffer size.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free;` immediately before `copy_to_user(input_address, id_blob, data.len)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that on invalid-length failures “copying the number of bytes firmware requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a failure guard in sev_ioctl_do_get_id2() to abort and clean up when the command returns an error or argp->error is unexpectedly set.
intent_record.what: An early-exit check was added after the preceding operation in sev_ioctl_do_get_id2(): if ret is nonzero or WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error) evaluates true, execution now jumps to the e_free cleanup label before attempting to use id_blob or copy data to userspace.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from continuing after a command failure or unexpected firmware-reported error state, ensuring allocated resources are cleaned up and avoiding copying potentially invalid or uninitialized ID blob data to userspace.

grouping_result.intent: Add a failure guard in sev_ioctl_do_get_id2() to abort and clean up when the command returns an error or argp->error is unexpectedly set.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds an error-path guard in sev_ioctl_do_get_id2() so userspace copying is aborted when the firmware/command reports failure, which addresses the root cause of using firmware-updated length data after a failed command.

candidates.rationale: This statement performs the userspace copy using data.len without first ensuring the PSP/firmware command succeeded. If firmware updated data.len on failure, this could copy beyond the allocated id_blob buffer to userspace.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement copies data.len bytes from the kernel buffer id_blob to userspace without first verifying that the preceding PSP/firmware command completed successfully. Because firmware could update data.len even on failure, this use of data.len could exceed the allocated id_blob size and leak out-of-bounds kernel memory to userspace.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2()` is fully shown, so the snippet is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present: after `ret = __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_GET_ID, &data, &argp->error);`, the code unconditionally trusts firmware-updated `data.len` and assigns `input.length = data.len;`. Then, if `id_blob` exists, it does `copy_to_user(input_address, id_blob, data.len)` without checking whether the command succeeded (`ret`) and without validating that `data.len` is still bounded by the originally allocated `input.length`. Since `id_blob` was allocated with `kmalloc(input.length, GFP_KERNEL);` before the command, a failed firmware command could still leave `data.len` larger than the allocated buffer, matching the stated root cause. There is no fix here such as gating the copy on successful command completion or capping the copy length to the original allocation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full allocation, firmware call, and copy-back logic. The vulnerable construct is present. The buffer is allocated with the user-provided size at lines 610-618: `id_blob = kmalloc(input.length, GFP_KERNEL);` and `data->len = input.length;`. After the firmware call at line 621, the code unconditionally trusts the firmware-updated length: `input.length = data->len;` (line 627). Then, if `id_blob` exists, it copies `data->len` bytes back to userspace at lines 635-636: `copy_to_user(..., id_blob, data->len)`. There is no check that `ret == 0` before using `data->len`, and no validation that `data->len` is <= the originally allocated `input.length`. This matches the root cause: on firmware/PSP command failure, `data->len` may be modified to a larger value, causing an out-of-bounds copy from the kernel buffer. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present and the fix is not yet included.
